source_row.rationale: The combination of marked hyperglycemia, positive ketones, bicarbonate below 18 mEq/L, and deep Kussmaul-type respirations is consistent with diabetic ketoacidosis, whose primary acid-base disturbance is metabolic acidosis. Option D is correct. The rapid deep respirations represent respiratory compensation rather than a primary respiratory alkalosis, and neither metabolic alkalosis nor respiratory acidosis fits the ketotic low-bicarbonate presentation.
source_row.source_detail: Endotext/NCBI Bookshelf — Diabetic Ketoacidosis, Clinical Manifestations and diagnostic tables: DKA includes hyperglycemia, ketonemia/ketonuria, metabolic acidosis with pH <7.3 and/or bicarbonate <18 mmol/L, and Kussmaul breathing described as deep, labored breathing. Endotext Diabetic Ketoacidosis entry current in 2026; diagnostic criteria and clinical manifestations live-rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A client with poorly controlled diabetes has a serum glucose of 420 mg/dL, positive serum ketones, a bicarbonate level of 16 mEq/L, and rapid deep respirations. Which acid-base disturbance is most consistent with this presentation?
